correctness.rationale: Integrated bridge covariance gives Var(J)=1/12 and Cov(J,B_s)=s(1-s)/2. With two interior distinct sites all sign atoms have positive probability, and global sign reversal makes the Bayes decoder odd; the odd functions on the sign square are exactly the span of the two signs. Thus the arcsine sign Gram matrix and the Gaussian mixed moment give the exact objective, not a restricted linear decoder. In logit coordinates, decomposing into sign sum and difference gives the two terms (1+h)w/(1+c) and h(w-1)/(1-c), divided by 4 pi(w+h)^2; this verifies the frozen rational expression. Its unconstrained w-critical point grows with c, and for rho>=1/3 the factor (1-rho)(1+rho)^2(3rho-1)/(8rho^2) and c<rho give strict merit loss for every w>1. For rho<=1/3 the Lipschitz bound for log cosh gives both amplitude ratios at least rho, allowing a strict upper bound by replacing c with 3rho/5. The sign of the resulting variance certificate reduces to 4(1-rho^2)^2(25-9rho^2)-3(5-rho^2)^2 = (5-rho^2)^2-(6rho^3-14rho)^2, the stated opposite-sign cubic factors with an overall minus sign. This bounds the low correlations strictly below 1/(6 pi), realized by the symmetric rho=1/2 design. For the reflected design the logarithmic derivative sign is Q(rho)-1; the positive term of Q'/Q is <1/(1-rho), showing strict decrease of Q from infinity to zero. Pinned and duplicate observations reduce to at most a single sign (variance explained at most 1/(8 pi)). For the real-valued benchmark, the conditional residual consists of independent bridges on three intervals, giving residual variance sum(length^3)/12, minimized uniquely at trisection by strict convexity. Independent double-precision bisection gives rho=0.5393616215470003, s=0.3503800627463755, and explained fraction 0.638028078245238.
